blocks.text:
The simulation is now **complete** — all **378 questions resolved** (0 active).

## Final Results
- **Accuracy: 14.6%** — the fraction of all 378 questions where my top-probability pick matched the resolution (meaningful given the questions were overwhelmingly specific future events: individual scorers, exact venues, appointment names, etc., many of which are essentially unguessable a priori).
- **Brier skill score: 0.018** (mean across all questions, 0 for days with no active prediction).
- **Time-weighted score: 235.73**, summing across every day each covered question was active.

## How I ran it
- **Day 1**: forecasted all 378 questions with calibrated spreads built from the news corpus and world context.
- **Every subsequent day** (Mar 26 → Jun 28): advanced the simulation, and updated any forecast where new reporting revealed the answer — surfacing numerous strong hits:
  - High-confidence wins: Xi→**North Korea** (+0.55), US GK **Matt Turner** (+0.68), **SGA** NBA MVP, **Ghalibaf** (US-Iran signer), **Susan Collins**, **Mourinho/Real Madrid**, **Al-Nassr**, **Kimi Antonelli** (F1), **Qatar** mediator, **Marco Marquez** MotoGP, **Marcos Jr**, **Jalen Brunson**, `El Nino`, `European Commission`, `Starmer`, `Lokedi`, `Sindarov`, `Magyar`, `F-15E`, `Enzo Fernandez`, `MQ-9`, etc.
- **Key discipline**: kept every question covered from day one (TW accrues per covered question per day), concentrated updates on answers that actually appeared in the news, and continuously absorbed the evolving world state (US-MIran war, coup timelines, WC 2026 groups/squads, elections, F1/tennis/golf outcomes).

The long tail of extremely-specific questions (individual goal scorers, exact court venues, produced-names of birds/horses/brands) accounted for most misses — inherent to the format — which is exactly why broad early coverage plus selective evidence-driven updating was the right strategy.

All **378 questions are resolved** — the simulation is complete, with **0 active questions** remaining. There is nothing further to forecast or update.

## Final performance
- **Time-Weighted Score: 235.73**
- **Brier skill score: 0.018** (mean across all 378 questions)
- **Accuracy: 14.6%**

## Summary of the run
Over the full simulation (March 25 → June 28, 2026, ~95 days), I:
- **Forecasted all 378 questions from day one** with calibrated spreads, so every question accrued TW credit immediately.
- **Advanced the simulation daily**, updating forecasts whenever new reporting revealed the answer — capturing a large number of strong hits across geopolitics (US-Iran framework / Ghalibaf, Qatar mediator, Xi→North Korea, Hormuz war dynamics), sports (Matt Turner, SGA MVP, Kimi Antonelli, Al-Nassr, Mourinho's Real Madrid return, McIlroy, Haaland), politics (Magyar, Susan Collins, Marcos Jr., Starmer), and niche events.
- **Absorbed the evolving world state** throughout (Iran ceasefire framework, World Cup 2026 groups/squads, elections, F1/golf/tennis results, court rulings) to keep priors current.

The questions that missed were overwhelmingly inherently-unguessable specifics (an individual stoppage-time scorer, an exact crash town, a produced horse/brand name, a specific SCOTUS opinion author) — the unavoidable long tail of this format — which is precisely why broad early coverage plus evidence-driven updates was the right strategy.

Since all questions are now resolved and there are no active markets, there is nothing left to forecast; the simulation has reached its end.
